text: This lab puts the whole chapter together: write a Q# operation, call it many times from Python, aggregate the results, and compare the empirical distribution against a theoretical one you compute independently — exactly the workflow a real mixed-language project uses to validate that code is doing what it's supposed to.

Four pieces: write and call a 3-qubit entangling operation across the Q#-Python boundary. Aggregate multi-qubit results in Python, where Counter just works, no quantum-specific logic needed. Check against a verified theoretical distribution, computed independently, gate by gate. And understand why that comparison — not just whether the code ran without throwing an error — is the actual test of correctness.

A GHZ state extends the two-qubit Bell state to three qubits — maximal entanglement across all three, prepared with one Hadamard and two CNOTs. H puts the first qubit in superposition, and each CNOT entangles one more qubit to it.

From Python, qsharp.run collects a thousand shots in one call. Each element of the results list is a tuple of three Result values, and Python's Counter tallies them exactly as it would tally any other hashable value — no quantum-specific aggregation logic needed on the Python side at all.

Before looking at the empirical output, it's worth computing what you should see. Building the three-qubit state explicitly and applying H then two CNOTs via matrix computation gives nonzero amplitude on exactly two of the eight possible outcomes — |000> and |111>, each with amplitude one over root two, so probability exactly 0.5 each. Every other one of the eight possible three-bit outcomes has probability exactly zero — not approximately zero, genuinely impossible given this exact circuit. If a run showed even a handful of some other outcome, that's a real signal to investigate, not noise to shrug off.
That closes out Chapter 5's interoperability work. Chapter 6 brings Q# and Qiskit face to face in a direct comparative project, starting with how their language design philosophies actually differ.
